key_insight: Regularized importance sampling breaks reward-shift invariance in policy gradients, and a covariance-based estimator restores the correct objective while clarifying when baselines and score centering help.
engineering_relevance: For RL post-training of large language models, this gives a practical rule for reducing bias and variance under off-policy updates with truncated, masked, or clipped importance ratios.
method: Reframe the policy gradient as a covariance between reward and importance-weighted score.
Use a group-mean baseline to center rewards at the sample level.
Apply score centering with the population mean when token-level importance sampling is used.
evidence_signal: The paper is a theoretical note that derives unbiased covariance estimators for both sequence-level and token-level importance sampling and compares their variance and bias properties.
watch_item: Do not assume baseline and score centering are interchangeable: with token-level importance sampling, using only a group-mean baseline under regularized ratios can introduce bias.
paper_title: Baselines and Score Centering in Policy Gradient Estimation
